title: quant-kernel-optimizer: fused-dequant kernels, fp8 path, and quant-aware batching/kv-cache
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Reduce runtime overhead and kernel-switching costs for quantized inference (INT8 and experimental FP8) and make continuous batching + KV cache work efficiently with fused dequant paths. Quantized workloads currently pay a penalty due to repeated dequantize->matmul->quantize roundtrips and suboptimal scheduling when mixing quant and non-quant requests. This PR implements three coordinated improvements: 1) fused dequant+matmul kernels for INT8 that avoid separate buffer materialization, 2) an experimental FP8 execution path with runtime kernel selection and fallbacks, and 3) a quant-aware batching and KV cache strategy to co-locate requests with compatible quant configs and persist quantized KV pages where safe.
Change summary:
- runtime/quant_kernels.cc/.h: added fused_dequant_gemm and fused_fp8_gemm kernels with AVX/AMX and CUDA code paths. New api: KernelDescriptor includes quant_mode and scale_metadata.
- runtime/scheduler.cc/.h: scheduler now groups pending requests by quantization signature (bitwidth + smoothquant id + scaling table hash) before building batches. Includes low-latency heuristic to prioritize fused-dequant kernels for small batches (1-8) to reduce tail latency.
- runtime/kv_cache.cc: KV cache now supports an optional quantized representation for keys/values with per-chunk scaling metadata and reference counting to allow safe reuse across requests. Added eviction guard to prevent reuse when smoothquant transient calibrations are active.
- third_party/smoothquant/: added calibration script (calibrate_smoothquant.py) and serialized layer-scale format (.sqf). Runtime loads .sqf and marks compatible models at load time.
- benchmarks/bench_quant_perf.py: new harness to run representative generation workloads and measure p50/p95 cost and throughput across quant configs.
- tests/: added unit tests for fused kernel numerics, scheduler grouping, and KV persistence semantics.
Benchmarks (measured on a 4xA100-hosted Dedicated cluster):
- INT8 fused-dequant kernel vs previous baseline: p95 latency (seq=512) improved 18% (from 76ms to 62ms), p50 improved 22%. Throughput for batched generation increased 1.4x at batch size 16. Token cost reduction estimated ~28% for steady-state workloads.
- FP8 path (experimental) shows comparable latency to INT8 in many layers but requires calibration; accuracy regression on GLUE-like evals <0.8% for test models after smoothquant.
- KV cache with quant persistence reduced per-request dequant ops by ~65% in long-context workloads, cutting tail latency by additional ~10% when combined with fused kernels.
Safety & compat:
- All new kernels have numeric unit tests and fallback to existing dequant->matmul path when: (a) model is not flagged as smoothquant-compatible, (b) calibration tables are missing/corrupt, or (c) runtime detects gradient-descent-trained layers with incompatible shapes.
- Feature gated: FP8 path must be enabled via --enable-fp8 on server start; experimental flag prevents accidental rollouts.
Checklist:
- [x] fused INT8 kernels implemented (C++ + CUDA)
- [x] FP8 experimental path implemented and gated
- [x] scheduler grouping and low-latency heuristic implemented
- [x] KV cache quant persistence implemented with eviction guards
- [x] calibration tooling and runtime loader for smoothquant tables
- [x] unit tests and integration benchmarks added
- [x] docs updated (in redwood-docs repo separate PR)
Rollout plan: staged rollout on Dedicated clusters: canary (10%) -> 33% -> 100% over one week, with automatic rollback if p95 regresses >5%.
Related: ENG-9241 (quant kernel roadmap), ENG-9310 (KV cache persist).

release_notes: Add fused INT8 dequant+GEMM kernels, experimental FP8 support, and quant-aware batching/kv-cache to reduce latency and per-token cost for quantized inference. Backwards-compatible and gated behind runtime flags.
notes_for_operators: Enable --enable-quant-cache to persist quantized KV pages; enable --enable-fp8 only for models that have been calibrated with the smoothquant tool. Monitor 'quant_sig' telemetry to validate grouping efficiency. Canary rollout recommended.
